header: THE PAX ANSWER (step 63a): from the question and the rows of the directory to the card the omnibar draws. My standing rule (26 Oct 2026): the ONE clean answer stands first as a single big bold statement (the number, the name, a count; amber "Not found" when it is not there), then the table, with no explanation and no red note (my rule, 31 Oct 2026). The card is the same one the hospital answers use (HospitalAnswerCard: headline, one sentence, table, bullets, red notes, folded details), so the screen needs no new component. Plain text only (React escapes it). Nothing here is invented. A number is shown only when it is a row of the table; a word read through a spelling slip is SAID ("read 'servise' as 'service'"); a name that merely shares some words is shown as "closest", never as the answer.

symbols.name: cards
doc: The pieces of a card, made for one directory. `directory` = EVERY row of the list, because which names share a department is read from the whole list (display.ts), not from the few rows shown. The table is Department | Location | PAX, the departments A to Z, with no column for plant or outside plant (my rule, 31 Oct 2026). A department (one place) with more than one number is ONE row: "40926 / 42043", the numbers in order.

symbols.name: answerPax
symbols.sig: export async function answerPax(typed: string, load: () => Promise<PaxRow[]>): Promise<PaxAnswer | null>
doc: The entry point of the omnibar's PAX route. I read the question FIRST (pure, no database), so only a question the route may take reads the table. `load` reads the rows with the application's own connection (never the model's read-only role). Returns null when the question is not a PAX question.
